qualitative.gate_2_reason: Commodity price taker lacking pricing power; cyclical spot salmon prices, biological shocks, and Norwegian resource-rent taxation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Essential Western Need, REJECT). World's largest salmon farmer is a structural commodity price-taker whose margins swing violently with global spot salmon prices, ocean biological shocks (sea lice, algae, water temperature), and severe Norwegian resource-rent tax levies (~47% marginal rate).
qualitative.evidence: Harvested record 559,000 tonnes in 2025 with revenue of €5.73B, yet Operational EBIT dropped from €829M (2024) to €727M (2025) purely due to falling global spot salmon prices (-12% industry volume surge). Upstream operations are subject to biological volatility and Norway's 25% resource-rent aquaculture tax (layered on top of 22% corporate tax), permanently compressing net returns on capital across the cycle.
